Hi Elena — thanks for taking the demo today. Quick recap and the asks we promised: 

1) Procurement path: you mentioned Procurement prefers a PO/invoice cadence but are open to card for smaller pilots. Can you confirm the default lane (PO vs corporate card) and any monthly card limits we should be aware of?

2) Vendor onboarding: please confirm the required onboarding artifacts (W9, certificate of insurance, vendor setup form). If AP needs any specific payee code or tax id fields on our side, let us know so we can populate them.

3) Marketplace: you said your Sourcing team tends to avoid third-party marketplaces for vendor management. Can you confirm whether listing on AWS/GCP marketplace would be a blocker for procurement?

Next steps we proposed on the call: 
- I’ll send a short summary and the deck we used.
- Naomi/Finance will confirm whether Redwood can accept a single PO for the pilot and timeline for vendor onboarding.

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + procurement questions

Hi Ben — great demo, appreciated the clarity. Answers inline: 

1) Default lane: Procurement prefers invoiced PO for anything > $5k net. For pilots under $5k we can use the corporate procurement card (Pcard). Our Pcard team enforces a monthly spend cap per vendor of $50k.

2) Vendor onboarding: we require the vendor setup form (attached), W9, and bank ACH details. Our AP team will also ask for a Certificate of Insurance for services. Expect vendor onboarding to take 2–3 weeks once all docs are received; if a vendor requires vendor vetting it can extend.

3) Marketplace: our Sourcing policy is conservative — we prefer direct vendor contracts. Listing on a cloud marketplace is not a blocker per se, but it complicates tax and procurement reporting. For this pilot, please plan for a direct PO/invoice path.

I attached the vendor setup form and looped in AP for any follow-ups.

Attachments: [Attachment: vendor-setup-form.xlsx (Excel)]

Cheers,
Elena Ortiz
Head of Procurement Operations | ProcureCo

Thanks for the flag, Ben. Quick answers from Finance: 

A) Yes — we can accept a ProcureCo PO with standard net30 terms for the pilot. To speed onboarding we need: completed vendor-setup-form, W9, ACH, and COI. If we receive all docs in one submission we can push vendor creation to Priority queue; realistic earliest vendor creation = 7 business days, typical = 10–15.

B) Commercial constraints: we can invoice for any amount but recommend splitting invoices if you expect monthly usage to exceed their Pcard cap. For deals expected >$50k/month we should default to PO with quarterly billing to simplify AP reconciliation.
